q: The method of Lyapunov functions proves asymptotic stability of an equilibrium x* if:
opts: A quadratic form V is positive definite and dV/dt ≤ 0
V is positive definite and dV/dt < 0 on a neighborhood of x*
V is negative definite along trajectories
The linearization has all eigenvalues with negative real part
exp: For asymptotic stability we need V > 0 and dV/dt < 0 (strictly negative definite) near x*. If only dV/dt ≤ 0, we get Lyapunov (not asymptotic) stability without LaSalle's invariance principle.
